articles.title: Moses Itauma v Filip Hrgović: IBF heavyweight championship – live
articles.summary: Itauma faces Hrgović for vacant IBF title. Reality check: just how good is Itauma? Reach out to Bryan on Bluesky or by email. Sam Noakes has scored the biggest win of his career, outclassing former world champion Denys Berinchyk to win a 10-round unanimous decision.
body: Here’s how Itauma and Hrgović measure up ahead of tonight’s main event. Itauma is the younger man by 13 years and gives away an inch and a half in height and three inches in reach, but he will enter the ring as the heavier fighter. The 21-year-old tipped the scales at 241.7lb, compared with 232.6lb for Hrgovic. The Croatian brings a significant edge in professional experience, having boxed 105 rounds to Itauma’s 31.
The waiting is over. The final instructions have been given by referee Howard Foster, the seconds are out and we’ll pick it up with round-by-round coverage from here!

The fighters are making their entrances for the main event. First out is Hrgović, emerging to Geni Kameni, the rousing Croatian nationalist anthem by the controversial rock singer Thompson. Now here comes Itauma, making his way to the ring in a black sleeveless vest to a medley of Sister Nancy’s Bam Bam and Crystal Waters’ Gypsy Woman (She’s Homeless). He’s moving with purpose, practically at a canter.

articles.title: European football: Elversberg stun Leverkusen in dream Bundesliga debut
articles.summary: Team from town of 13,000 shock 2024 champions. Juventus 2-0 Parma; Sevilla 1-3 Atlético Madrid. The Bundesliga newcomers Elversberg began their first top-flight campaign in style, stunning Bayer Leverkusen with an impressive 3-2 home victory on Saturday.
body: Lukas Petkov and Cole Campbell scored within 60 seconds of each other to put Elversberg 2-0 up before the 10-minute mark. David Mokwa added another early in the second half in front of 9,307 delirious fans.

Patrik Schick and Christian Kofane pulled late goals back, but it was not enough to prevent a famous victory for Elversberg, as they embarrassed a team who won the title in 2024 without losing a game.

The town of Elversberg has a population of just 13,000, making it the smallest settlement to have ever hosted a Bundesliga side. Their ground, the Ursapharm-Arena, has a reduced capacity while upgrades are made to meet the German top flight’s stadium criteria.
“It’s an indescribable day,” the Elversberg captain, Lukas Pinckert, told Sky. “We worked hard to earn the right to play in this league. The victory is deserved. I am incredibly proud of the team.”

articles.title: Newcastle show there's plenty of life after Tonali
articles.summary: Newcastle United sold Sandro Tonali to Tottenham Hotspur, but the club look to have reinvested the money wisely following United's 2-0 win in north London.
body: Sandro Tonali anticipated being "more nervous" than usual about coming up against former club Newcastle United for the first time.
You suspect the Tottenham Hotspur midfielder felt a little sick following their 2-0 defeat on Saturday evening.
"Sandro, what's the score?" the away fans taunted in the closing stages as the substituted Italian looked on.
This bruising loss was certainly not the reunion Tonali had in mind after joining Spurs for a fee worth up to £100m last month.

articles.title: Carrick dismisses ‘lazy’ Manchester United criticism and defends Fernandes’ leadership
articles.summary: Manager says opening-day defeat just ‘one game’ United to be without Carlos Baleba against Ipswich. Michael Carrick has said it was “lazy and easy” to say everything was wrong with Manchester United after the opening-day defeat at Hull.
body: United lost 2-0 in a tame display and the manager was asked whether his captain, Bruno Fernandes, and Youri Tielemans, Belgium’s captain, had shown the leadership that might have affected the performance and result.

“It’s one game,” Carrick said. “I think there’s enough leadership in our dressing room that we’ll have it throughout the season. Just because we lose a game doesn’t just mean leadership [is the reason]. I got ‘passion’ thrown at me after the game; it’s not just that. You lose two set plays like we did [for the goals], it changes the game.”

Carrick was asked what the reason was for the performance. “You’ve watched football a long time, right? Teams lose games and win games, and it’s not just because you try or you don’t try. There’s all sorts of different reasons. I don’t have to give you the total reason, because we know what we’re trying to improve on.”

articles.title: Lavish spending fails to fix Tottenham’s big issue – the lack of soul and spine | Jonathan Liew
articles.summary: It might be too early to push the panic button but Roberto De Zerbi faces a huge task if he is to turn Spurs around. Time for Tottenham to start panicking? This is, of course, a subtle trick question. Tottenham is one of those clubs that never actually stops panicking.
body: You could intuit that sense of encrusted resignation pretty much from the moment Anthony Elanga’s improvised shot kissed the post and trickled over the line to give Newcastle the lead. Since beating Aston Villa 4-1 in late 2024, Tottenham have gone behind 44 times in all competitions and come back to win precisely zero of them. There is something innate and endemic here, a chronic case of Long Tottenham for which – despite the new coach, the new leadership structure and more than a third of a billion pounds in transfer fees – there remains no proven cure. Yoane Wissa’s clincher was of zero surprise to anyone.

articles.title: £300m spent, bottom of the table... but Spurs boss De Zerbi 'not angry'
articles.summary: Having spent more than £300m in the summer, Tottenham find themselves bottom of the Premier League, without a point or a goal, but boss Roberto de Zerbi remains optimistic.
body: Tottenham manager Roberto de Zerbi said he was "not angry" and there was "no panic" after his side's second loss in two games left them bottom of the Premier League – but it was a depressingly familiar story for the club's fans.
Goals from Anthony Elanga and Yoane Wissa in a 10-minute second-half spell gave Newcastle a 2-0 victory, with thousands of Spurs supporters heading for the exits early.
They have every reason to be annoyed as they have now seen only three home league wins from their past 23 matches at their superb stadium.
Seventeenth in the Premier League in 2024-25, 17th in 2025-26, only avoiding relegation on the final day, but this season was meant to be different.

articles.title: Dan Campbell backs Jake Bates after missed PATs: 'He'll be fine'
articles.summary: INDIANAPOLIS — After Detroit Lions kicker Jake Bates missed a pair of extra points in the team's 25-16 preseason win against the Indianapolis Colts on Saturday, Aug. 29, coach Dan Campbell said he isn't worried about his kicker's outlook going into the regular season.
body: Bates also missed a 55-yard attempt in last week's win over the Washington Commanders and had a relatively inconsistent training camp.
"No, I'm not worried about Bates. He just pushed them a little bit. He'll be fine. He'll be fine," Campbell said.

Bates joined the Lions during the 2024 offseason. His three camps to date have all been somewhat up and down. But he shook off some struggles in his rookie training camp to put together a sensational rookie season, during which he went 54-for-56 on extra points and 26-for-29 on field goals; he went 6-for-8 from beyond 50 yards and was 7-for-8 from 40-49 yards, while going a perfect 13-for-13 from inside 40. He also made three game-winning kicks.

Last season, Bates' field-goal percentage regressed from 89.7% to 79.4%, with most of his misses coming from 50-plus (4-for-9). He was 23-for-25 from inside 40 yards in 2025 and was still rock-solid on extra points, missing just two of his 56 attempts. He missed as many extra points on Saturday as he did all of last season.

29, coach Dan Campbell said he isn't worried about his kicker's outlook going into the regular season.
Bates also missed a 55-yard attempt in last week's win over the Washington Commanders and had a relatively inconsistent training camp.

articles.title: Dubois beats Moore to keep Baumgardner in picture
articles.summary: Caroline Dubois coasts to victory over Amelia Moore in Birmingham to defend her WBC and WBO lightweight titles and stay on course for a blockbuster meeting with Alycia Baumgardner.
body: Caroline Dubois coasted to victory over Amelia Moore to defend her WBC and WBO lightweight titles and stay on course for a blockbuster meeting with unified super-featherweight champion Alycia Baumgardner in 2027.
Dubois dominated the fight at BP Pulse Arenain Birmingham and knocked Moore down in the fifth round but was unable to find the decisive blow against the dogged American.
The British fighter won on unanimous judges' decision, 99-90 99-90 98-91 ahead on the scorecards.

Dubois was heavy favourite for this fight and never looked less than in control, although her reliance on power and presence rather than speed ensured it went the distance to a long, inevitable conclusion.

articles.title: Sparks claim Nye off waivers; let go of Martin, Pili
articles.summary: LOS ANGELES -- The Sparks made more moves on their roster as the 2026 season winds down. Aaliyah Nye was claimed off waivers by the Sparks after the Atlanta Dream let her go. Nye was drafted by the Toronto Tempo in the expansion draft but was cut by the team before the season started.
body: Kate Martin was signed to a regular contract but bizarrely enough, didn't nearly play as much as she did when she was in a developmental deal. She has been waived to make room for Nye. Martin ended up playing 17 games with the Sparks, averaging 2.3 points per game. She scored a season-high 11 points against the Tempo in mid-May.

Alissa Pili was signed to a developmental deal around the same time they brought Martin up to the main roster. After playing Pili for five games, they have decided to release her. She averaged 2.0 points and 2.2 boards per game.

In a corresponding move, the Sparks signed Ndjakalenga Mwenentanda to a developmental deal. Mwenentanda went undrafted last spring after playing college ball in Texas and Vanderbilt. The 6'2" guard played five games this season for the Golden State Valkyries.
The Sparks (14-25) resume play on Sunday against the Storm in Seattle.

articles.title: Fery's dreams of maiden ATP Tour title ended in Winston-Salem Open final
articles.summary: Arthur Fery's hopes of landing his maiden ATP Tour title at Winston-Salem Open was ended in emphatic fashion by Peruvian Ignacio Buse on Saturday.
body: From 3-3 in the first set, Fery lost six straight games before eventually going down 6-3 6-2 to Buse.
The promising 22-year-old clinched his second trophy of the season having lifted his maiden tour-level trophy at the ATP 500 event in Hamburg.
Fery was aiming to add to his already memorable season having reached the semi-finals at Wimbledon and he is set for a new career high Monday.
With his spot in the Winston-Salem final, 24-year-old Fery has moved up to a new career high of No 33 in the live rankings, overtaking Cameron Norrie as the British No 1 in doing so.

articles.title: College football analyst doubts Dae’Quan Wright will ever take the field for LSU
articles.summary: One of the more bizarre developments of the college football offseason involves former Cleveland Browns tight end Dae’Quan Wright returning to college football. He is set to transfer and join the LSU Tigers this season.
body: Wright played in preseason games for the Browns before an injunction granted him eligibility. He decided to leave Cleveland and head to Baton Rouge. Wright isn’t the only former NFL player attempting to return to college football, either. The question now is whether he will actually play after the SEC threatened sanctions against LSU.
One college football analyst isn’t so sure that will happen. Paul Finebaum provided his thoughts on the situation and thinks LSU should reconsider.
MORE: What does UNC Tar Heels week zero win mean for Bill Belichick?

“I just think that there will be too many things that start happening … This is a very narrow path. It’s completely different, but like what the Big 12 tried, but I think the sentiment is going to really be against him … I think LSU has to decide if this is really worth staking whatever is left of our reputation.” Finebaum said.

articles.title: De Zerbi highlights biggest problem at Spurs as Carra slams 'worst start'
articles.summary: Roberto De Zerbi believes changing the mentality at Tottenham is his biggest challenge after Sky Sports' Jamie Carragher said their start to the season "couldn't have gone any worse" following defeat to Newcastle.
body: Tottenham have lost their first two Premier League games without scoring a goal and sit at the bottom of the league despite spending £320m in the transfer market this summer.

De Zerbi's side had been better than Newcastle until Anthony Elanga struck the opener midway through the second half, with Spurs unable to respond and conceding another when Yoane Wissa hooked in from close range.
Asked whether mentality was the biggest issue he faces, De Zerbi said: "You are right, yes. It's the biggest problem, it's the biggest challenge, the biggest target is to find the right mentality.

"Unfortunately you can't buy the mentality in the transfer market. Football is like magic: you can change many players in one window of the transfer market, and you can find the balance immediately, or you need more time. I would like to achieve this target quickly, as soon as possible, because it's crucial to play football.

articles.summary: Sunderland, Crystal Palace, Bournemouth, Brighton, Celtic and Hearts have learned the details of their Europa League and Conference League fixtures this season.
body: The league-phase draws for both competitions were made on Friday, with Europa League clubs set to play eight matches, while Conference League sides will play six - an equal number home and away - between September 2026 and January 2027.
Sunderland reached Europe for the first time in 53 years and will travel to the San Siro to face AC Milan, while Bournemouth, in their first European competition, will also host the Italian club.

Celtic will host Marseille and travel to Marco Silva's Benfica among their eight Europa League matches, while Crystal Palace, last season's Conference League winners, will host LaLiga side Real Sociedad and visit France's Lyon.
